channel.title: Honolulu Civil Beat - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Honolulu Civil Beat (civilbeat.org)

item.title: Makana Eyre: Qualms About Celebrating The Moana Surfrider
item.description: Yes, the Waikīkī property about to celebrate its 125th anniversary is a stately icon. But it also tells an uglier story of who profited from the island's transformation.

item.title: Word Flower: Feb. 23
item.description: Start your week off right with our spelling game.

item.title: Kaua‘i Residents Worry 148-unit Housing Project Will ‘Kill’ Kōloa Town
item.description: The Garden Isle needs more housing but Kōloa residents worry the proposed project is too big, will harm the environment and won’t be within reach of community members.

item.title: More Local Food? These State Agencies Aren’t Buying It
item.description: Few departments met the official 10% goal last year. While cost, quality and lack of consistent supply are concerns, the current pace doesn't bode well for the larger push to wean the islands off imported food.

item.title: Climate Funding Under New Hawai‘i Tax Could Be Cut By Millions
item.description: Legislation to instead charge a per-passenger fee would recoup less than half of all the green fee revenues cruise ships were expected to generate.

item.title: HMSA Proposal: Hawaiʻi Health Care Could See Radical Transformation
item.description: Changes could touch 760,000 HMSA members and their doctors.

item.title: Denby Fawcett: My $54 Lesson In Social Media Scams
item.description: A bipartisan bill pending in Congress would require social media platforms to first verify a company’s business credentials before allowing it to advertise.

item.title: Word Row: Feb. 24
item.description: Take a few minutes to challenge your brain with our popular version of Wordle.

item.title: The Human Cost Of Waiting For Mental Health Care In Hawaiʻi
item.description: Long delays in access show up in families, in emergency rooms, and in communities across our state.

item.title: Honolulu Investigator Obstructed His Own Criminal Case, Hawaiʻi AG Says
item.description: The charges come after a Civil Beat report revealed Steve Alm's office knew about the allegations, botched an investigation and invited the employee back to work.
